findings.check: Database access: the migration runner (all-or-nothing writes, failure handling)
findings.title: The 12 s guard of the migration command stays armed during the migration and kills it with the message 'no answer from the database'
findings.where: app/server/db/migrate.js lines 149-152 (timer) and 189 (the only clearTimeout); app/Dockerfile line 15 (migrate runs before the server at every start)
findings.evidence: Lines 149-152: `const timer = setTimeout(() => { process.stderr.write("migrate: refused: no answer from the database\n"); process.exit(2); }, CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS + 2000);` with CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000 (line 16). `grep -n "setTimeout\|clearTimeout\|CONNECT_TIMEOUT" server/db/migrate.js` prints the single clearTimeout at line 189, inside `finally` of main(), after `await migrate(...)`. The guard is meant for E8 (design: the database is unreachable or silent, one line within 12 s), but it is not cleared after the connection and the first statement have succeeded, so it also covers every later migration file and the password step.
findings.item: Q3 (a failure is handled and named correctly); Q10 (the message tells the truth)
findings.recommendation: In app/server/db/migrate.js main(): clear the timer as soon as the session is connected and the advisory-lock query has answered (or arm it only around connectPgSession and the first query), so a long but healthy migration is not killed and the wrong message is not printed. Add an int test in app/test/int/migrate.test.js with a migration file that sleeps longer than the guard. State stays consistent today (the server rolls back the open transaction when the session ends and releases the advisory lock), so this is Medium, not High, while only 0001_init.sql exists; it becomes a crash loop in Docker (migrate && start) as soon as one migration needs more than about 12 s.

findings.check: Database access: error classes of the two drivers (toDbError), honest /api/health
findings.title: toDbError takes any five-character upper-case code for an SQLSTATE: Node codes EPIPE and EBUSY become E_DB_QUERY and /api/health says db "ok" for a broken connection
findings.evidence: Line 48: `/^[0-9A-Z]{5}$/.test(code) && !code.startsWith("08")` gives E_DB_QUERY. Run with Node 22: `EPIPE E_DB_QUERY`, `EBUSY E_DB_QUERY`, `ECONNRESET E_DB_DOWN`, `ETIMEDOUT E_DB_DOWN`, `ECONNREFUSED E_DB_DOWN`, `08006 E_DB_DOWN`, `57P01 E_DB_QUERY`. health.js lines 60-62: on E_DB_QUERY the body gets `db: "ok"` and `role` from roleState. A socket error `write EPIPE` (the peer closed a pooled connection) carries code 'EPIPE', so the health answer is 503 with `"db":"ok"` while the connection is down. `grep -rn 'toDbError\|EPIPE' app/test` finds no test of this function by name or of an errno code.
findings.item: Q3 (failure handled correctly); Q10 (an honest, understandable status)
findings.recommendation: In app/server/db/index.js toDbError: accept an SQLSTATE only when the error comes from the server (the pg DatabaseError has a `severity` field and PGlite's error too) or exclude Node errno codes (a code that starts with 'E' followed by letters only, or `typeof err.errno === 'number'`/`err.syscall`). Add unit cases for EPIPE, EBUSY, 57P01 and 08006 in a new app/test/unit test, and a health case for a driver error with code EPIPE that must answer db "down". Decide separately whether class 57 (operator intervention: admin shutdown, cannot connect now) should read as down: today 57P01 also gives db "ok".

findings.check: Recorded design against the code: the role selfcheck statement
findings.title: The design of the app skeleton gives another SELFCHECK_SQL than the code; the membership rule that the code adds is written in no document
findings.evidence: Design line 384: `SELFCHECK_SQL = "select rolsuper, rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname = session_user"`. Code: `select coalesce(bool_or(rolsuper), true) as rolsuper, coalesce(bool_or(rolbypassrls), true) as rolbypassrls from pg_roles where pg_has_role(session_user, oid, 'MEMBER')`, with a comment saying a role the session can become by `set role` counts as its own. `grep -rln pg_has_role docs decisions` prints nothing. The code is the stricter one (it also refuses a sai_app that bypasses row security), so the behaviour is safe; the document is what is outdated.
findings.item: Q12 (a divergence from the recorded design without a new record); documents match the files
findings.recommendation: DOC-UPDATER: amend docs/design/REQ-108-109-app-skeleton.md section 4.4 (line 384) (and any line of the same document that repeats the one-row reading) to the membership reading, with the reason from the code comment, or record the change as a decision record (decisions/) if it was taken on purpose after the design; name which.

findings.check: AP-014: one mechanism in all neighbouring places
findings.title: Copies of one constant or one error answer stand in several files without a pin: the 4000 ms deadline (4 places), the language list, the 503 server_config body
findings.where: app/server/node-main.js line 17 and app/server/db/index.js line 61; app/server/routes/health.js line 5; app/server/app.js line 199; app/server/routes/demo.js line 20 and app/public/shared/i18n/lang.js line 6; app/api/index.js lines 48-55 and app/server/http/errors.js
findings.evidence: node-main.js line 17 `const SELFCHECK_DEADLINE_MS = 4000;` redefines the constant that db/index.js line 61 exports under the same name; health.js line 5 `HEALTH_DEADLINE_MS = 4000`; app.js line 199 passes the literal `connectTimeoutMs: 4000`. demo.js line 20 `TEXT_LANGS = Object.freeze(["ru", "kk", "en"])` is SOURCE_LANGS of lang.js (same file already imports pickLang from it), so a fourth language added to lang.js would not be read as a text object by inLanguage. api/index.js builds `JSON.stringify({ error: "server_config" })` by hand with its own headers while errors.js has the code server_config and errorBody; the 503 of the entry also skips the app's header and request-id middleware (on Vercel vercel.json adds the headers, so the visible effect today is only the missing X-Request-Id).
findings.item: Q12 (one mechanism in all neighbouring places, AP-014)
findings.recommendation: Import SELFCHECK_DEADLINE_MS from db/index.js in node-main.js and name one constant for the 4000 ms of app.js; import SOURCE_LANGS in routes/demo.js instead of TEXT_LANGS (the test demo-parity already compares the result with the tools implementation); build the entry's 503 with errorBody('server_config') and ERROR_STATUS from errors.js.

summary: app/ is built as its records say: the layers are clean and held by a rule test (server imports only server and public/shared; pg and PGlite once each; nothing of tools/ or test/ at run time), the selfcheck stands inside every database statement, the migration runner keeps its all-or-nothing promise, one function sits behind one explicit rewrite on Vercel, and the pinned engine and the two office ports match their sources byte for byte with checks in app `npm run check` and in app.yml paths. The head's 6 changed files break no boundary. Findings: 0 Critical, 0 High, 4 Medium (the migrate guard that kills a long migration, toDbError reading EPIPE/EBUSY as an SQLSTATE so health says db ok, the 886-line mountSurvey, the design's outdated selfcheck statement), 2 Low (dead withPlatform/readText/codes, unpinned copies of constants). 16 checks done, 6 not done (all for the rules of this PC or other dimensions); every result of a test run rests on the GitHub records of app runs 45031353708 and 45034277809, never on a local run.
